packet.explanation: Testing discipline means making sure your code works not just for the examples you expect, but also for edge cases, invalid inputs, and all possible scenarios—because one passing test doesn't prove your code is correct.
packet.strategy: Testing discipline ensures reliable software by systematically verifying correctness. First, write multiple test cases, not just one, to avoid overconfidence from a single success. Check boundary cases (like minimum/maximum values) where bugs are most likely. Include negative tests to confirm the system handles invalid input safely. Finally, use property checks to validate general behaviors across many inputs, ensuring consistency beyond specific examples.
